newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: C&W to bid for Singapore telecoms license.
newsitem.headline: C&W to bid for Singapore telecoms license.

text.p: British telecommunications giant Cable and Wireless (C&W) said on Tuesday it would make a bid for a full telecoms licence to operate in Singapore when the industry is degregulated in April 2000.

Richard Goswell, C&W's Southeast Asia and Pacific chief executive, told Reuters his company was looking for a suitable partner or partners for the bid, but had not yet decided who it would link up with.
Asked if C&W would bid for a full licence to compete with the current monopoly telephone company, Singapore Telecom, Goswell replied: "Yes."
"You will definitely see Cable and Wireless somewhere (in the bidding process)," he said.
Asked which partners C&W would link up with in the license bid, he repled: "I comment on that at this stage."
He said in reply to a question the terms of the bid would be announced before the end of March 1997. "I'm sure there will be information in the market place before then (about the bid)," he added.

Brian Smith, group chairman of C&W plc, told Reuters his company might bid with the other members of the MobileOne consortium with which C&W is launching Singapore's second mobile telephone network next year.
MobileOne comprises C&W, Hong Kong Telecommunications Co Ltd, Keppel Corp and Singapore Press Holdings Ltd.
The Singapore government said in September it would allow at least one, and possibly two, new operators to compete directly with the current domestic telephone monopoly Singapore Telecom from 2000.
The first stage of the pre-qualification process for the licence would be held on March 1, 1997.
